html:
In 279 BCE a large army of Celtic Gauls led by a chief named Brennus invaded Greece, forced the pass of Thermopylae and attacked the great sanctuary of Delphi. They were driven back with heavy losses.

The Gauls had already broken into Macedon, where they killed the king, Ptolemy Keraunos. A Greek alliance of Aetolians, Boeotians, Athenians, Phocians and others held them at Thermopylae, the same narrow pass where the Spartans had fought the Persians in 480 BCE. As then, the invaders found a mountain path around the Greek position.

Brennus then marched on Delphi, home of the oracle and its treasures. The Greeks later told how Apollo defended his shrine with a winter storm, an earthquake and falling rocks. Whatever happened, the defenders, above all the Aetolians, beat the Gauls back. Brennus was wounded and is said to have killed himself, and the army fell apart on the retreat.

The Aetolian League gained great prestige and control of Delphi. Other Gauls crossed into Asia Minor and settled there, becoming the Galatians.
sum: In 279 BCE a large army of Celtic Gauls led by a chief named Brennus invaded Greece, forced the pass of Thermopylae and attacked the great sanctuary of Delphi. They were driven back with heavy losses.
